name: Should I build an addition or a detached ADU in my backyard?

mainEntity.name: When is a room addition better than a detached accessory unit?
mainEntity.text: When is a room addition better than a detached accessory unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: The better option depends on how you plan to live on the property. If you want the new space to function like part of the main home, an addition usually makes more sense because it creates a seamless layout and can improve daily use immediately. If the goal is rental income, guest privacy, or a separate workspace, a detached ADU may be the stronger choice. Detached units can also preserve the main house’s footprint, but they use yard space differently and require a separate design strategy. A room addition may be more efficient if you want to upgrade the kitchen, add a bathroom, or create a larger primary suite without changing how the property is used. Homeowners should compare long-term value, privacy, site coverage, and whether the existing house can support an integrated expansion. In dense neighborhoods, the best option is often the one that solves the main lifestyle problem with the least disruption.
acceptedAnswer.description: A room addition is better when you want more living space connected to the main house, such as a primary suite, family room, or expanded kitchen. A detached ADU is better when privacy, rental use, or separate occupancy matters most. The choice depends on lot size, intended use, and how much of the yard you want to keep.
